name: scenario-expedition
flow: an expedition: undertaken off the charted lanes, a waypoint looked over, finished
description: A scenario of the suite (suites/scenarios.json): the long haul's expedition beat (b7a) on its own. The character leaves the charted lane after a clipped distress call (Undertake an Expedition), looks over what she finds (Explore a Waypoint, whose strong hit offers a mark or momentum) and ends the journey with the card's Finish (a scripted progress roll). The seed's sector has map data, so the place she sets out for becomes a place, and the finish docks her there.
persona: You play Mira Kestrel (she/her), a courier-hunter who flies her own ship, the Kobayashi IV, alone. You are a careful, plain-spoken player: short first-person lines, one or two sentences, and you read what the narrator says before you act again.
goal: Play one short scene by walking the beats below, in order, one at a time. Each turn you are told which beat is current and what the observer sees of it. Do what that beat asks; an observer decides when it is done and moves you on.
playerNotes: Where a beat gives words to type, use exactly those words.

What you type is in the fiction: what Mira does or says, and nothing else. Never write a move's name, a stat or a rule word in it — no "Face Danger", no "roll", no "milestone", no "mark progress" — and never say what move a line is. The table reads your line and decides.

A beat that needs a roll gets it from a plain line. If the narrator answers without a roll and a card offers a "Roll …" button for what you were doing, press it — buttons may name moves. If nothing is offered, say what Mira does once more, in other words, still in the fiction.
Only when the observer's note for the beat says LAST RESORT may you name the move, in the words the note gives, in one line.
When a roll goes badly and a card asks how you pay, choose one of its buttons before anything else — and answer any card that follows from it.
If a card offers "Keep the result", press it, unless the current beat tells you to burn momentum.

Mira has her background vow on her sheet, to find the lost colony ship Verity's Hope, which no beat touches. Wherever a card or a dropdown asks which vow, choose the one this scene is about, not that one.

A roll does not end a beat, and neither does an answer: each turn the observer's note says what it sees of the beat. When it says the beat is NOT done, do not wait for it to move you on — do what the beat asks again, in other words.
Do not press buttons no beat calls for (rewards, portraits, "Play" and "Stop") unless a card is in the way of play.
If the narrator has not answered yet, wait rather than repeat yourself.

beats.title: Begin a Session
beats.tell: Type !begin-session. In the window that opens leave vignette unticked and press Begin.

beats.title: Undertake an Expedition; Explore a Waypoint; Finish the Expedition
beats.tell: A distress call is repeating from somewhere off the charted lanes — a hauler's, clipped short each time — and you mean to find where it comes from. Three things, in order. (1) In a line of play, take the Kobayashi IV off the charted lane and out into uncharted space along the call's bearing — a short run, to the source of the distress call. A roll should follow, and a card headed Expedition says a journey is begun and its progress marked. If the roll costs you, settle the card it gives you (choose one of its buttons); if it misses and no journey is begun, make the crossing again. (2) In another line of play, look over what you have come to out there: say how you go over the place, and what you are looking for. A roll should follow: if a card then offers "Mark expedition progress", press it; if it offers nothing to choose, there is nothing to press; if it costs you, settle its card. (3) Press "🗺 Finish the Expedition" on the newest Expedition card: you have reached the source of the call. The beat is done when the observer's note says the expedition is finished.
beats.playerTitle: Follow a distress call off the charts, look over what you find, and come to the end of it
beats.lastResort: say that you undertake an expedition to the source of the distress call — or, once one is under way, that you explore the waypoint you have reached

beats.title: Where the journey ended
beats.tell: @scene Where is the Kobayashi IV now? — type it exactly so. The narrator answers plainly.
beats.playerTitle: Ask where the ship is now

vows.name: Find the lost colony ship Verity's Hope

rehearsal.text: I take the Kobayashi IV off the charted lane and follow the clipped distress call's bearing out into the dark, a short run to wherever it is coming from.

move.target: the source of the distress call

rehearsal.text: I bring her in slow and go over the place the call is coming from, looking for whoever sent it.
@scene Where is the Kobayashi IV now?
